item.title: Jaguars knock off Bengals, who lose Ja'Marr Chase (concussion)
item.description: Trevor Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown to lead the visiting Jacksonville Jaguars past the Cincinnati Bengals 22-17 on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Trevor Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown to lead the visiting Jacksonville Jaguars past the Cincinnati Bengals 22-17 on Sunday. It was the first time Lawrence defeated Joe Burrow in four career meetings. Bhayshul Tuten ran 17 times for 73 yards while Chris Rodriguez Jr. added a 25-yard touchdown run for the Jaguars (3-1). Burrow was 39-of-54 passing for 428 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. Tee Higgins caught 11 passes for 157 yards while Chase Brown caught 11 passes for 71 yards for the Bengals (2-2). The Jaguars thought they had iced the game on a third-down pass from Lawrence to Parker Washington but replay brought a 39-yard gain back and ruled Washington's heel out of bounds near midfield. The Bengals and Burrow drove to the Jacksonville 21-yard line but on fourth-and-10, a pass for Brown came up short. On second down, Burrow missed an open Mike Gesicki in the end zone for the potential go-ahead score. The Bengals played the second half without star receiver Ja'Marr Chase, who was knocked out of the game with concussion symptoms. He had three catches for 27 yards. With 12 minutes left in the second quarter, Chase took a pass from Joe Burrow at the Jacksonville 30 and had his facemask turned by corner Jarrian Jones. As soon as Jones let go, linebacker Ventrell Miller lowered his helmet and hit Chase in the head, driving the receiver's head into the turf. Chase made it up on his own power, was examined in the tent and went to the locker room for concussion evaluation before being ruled out at halftime. The officiating crew of referee Alex Moore called 24 accepted penalties, including 16 in the first-half penalties in the first half, most in the NFL this season for a half. Each team had touchdown runs wiped out by holding calls. Cincinnati's Samaje Perine had a 14-yard run by a Dylan Fairchild hold while Jacksonville's Tuten had a 44-yard run nullified by Ezra Cleveland. Tuten later had a 3-yard TD run negated by a hold. The Bengals played the game without starting safety Bryan Cook (ankle). Russ Yeast and PJ Jules filled in for Cook. Jacksonville took advantage of a Jourdan Lewis interception of Burrow and a 45-yard return to the Cincinnati 18 to score the game's first touchdown. Lawrence threw a pass over a trio of Cincinnati defenders to a wide-open Brian Thomas Jr. for a 13-3 lead just before halftime. Cincinnati opened the second half with a 12-play, 67-yard drive that ended with Burrow's 15-yard touchdown strike over the middle to Gesicki. With Jacksonville leading 16-10, the Bengals were on the brink of taking the lead. Burrow hit Higgins for 26 yards down to the Jacksonville 10. But on the next play, Burrow threw a pass for Mitch Tinsley that Foyesade Oluokun stepped in front of for an interception. --Field Level Media

item.title: Former Anthropic researcher Coxon to testify at New York City AI hearing, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon will testify at a New York City hearing on artificial intelligence, Bloomberg News reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former Anthropic researcher [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"Jacob Coxon"] will testify at a New York City hearing on artificial intelligence, Bloomberg News reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Coxon will appear at the request of New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin, who has urged AI whistleblowers to testify as city lawmakers weigh a package of bills aimed at establishing safeguards around the technology, the report said. Coxon quit Anthropic last month, [USN:L6N4520JB TEXT:"issuing"] warnings that the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade" and accusing his former employer and OpenAI of "gambling with our lives." Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

item.title: Cowboys stun Texans 34-30 behind CeeDee Lamb, huge second half
item.description: Javonte Williams ran for three touchdowns in the second half and CeeDee Lamb scored on his 17th reception of the game with 40 seconds remaining as the Dallas Cowboys collected a high-voltage 34-30 comeback victory over the host Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Javonte Williams ran for three touchdowns in the second half and CeeDee Lamb scored on his 17th reception of the game with 40 seconds remaining as the Dallas Cowboys collected a high-voltage 34-30 comeback victory over the host Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon. Lamb posted a career-best 17 receptions and totaled 189 yards to help Dallas overcome a 10-point halftime deficit. Jason Witten (18 in 2012) is the only Dallas player to have more receptions in a game. Dak Prescott completed 32 of 45 passes for 335 yards and Williams had 62 yards on 19 carries for the Cowboys (2-2). C.J. Stroud was 21-of-31 passing for 347 yards and two touchdowns for the Texans (0-4), who have lost their first four games for the first time since 2020. Houston's Nico Collins caught seven passes for 118 yards and two scores after a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Woody Marks rushed for a score. Stroud guided the Texans on a nine-play, 87-yard drive to take a 30-27 lead with 2:23 left. The pivotal play was on third-and-14 from the Dallas 27-yard line. Stroud threw a short pass to tight end Dalton Schultz at the 25. His lateral to David Montgomery was good for 19 more yards to the Cowboys' 6. Marks scored on the next play. Prescott then drove Dallas 74 yards on 11 plays, eventually connecting with Lamb for the winning points. Dallas trailed by 10 at the break but KaVontae Turpin opened the third quarter with a 48-yard kickoff return to the Texans' 49. Four plays later, Williams scored on an 8-yard run to bring the Cowboys 16-13. Houston answered with its own impressive kickoff return as Jaylin Noel went 53 yards to the Dallas 38. Four plays later, Stroud tossed a 22-yard touchdown pass to Collins to give the Texans a 23-13 advantage with 10:50 left in the quarter. Later in the quarter, Williams scored from the 1 as Dallas pulled within three with 6:49 left. On their next possession, the Cowboys drove 81 yards on 14 plays with Williams scoring on a 2-yard run to give Dallas its first lead at 27-23 with 11:17 left in the game. Stroud threw a touchdown pass to Collins and Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked three field goals as the Texans led 16-6 at halftime. Houston took the opening kickoff and went 85 yards on eight plays. Stroud hit Collins for 45 yards at the outset of the drive and later connected on a 7-yard scoring pass to Collins. Dallas responded with Brandon Aubrey's 39-yard field goal with 5:10 left before Fairbairn was good from 51 yards to give the Texans a 10-3 advantage with 1:49 remaining. Aubrey drilled a 50-yard field goal to bring the Cowboys within 10-6 with 12:30 left in the half. Fairbairn added field goals of 39 and 54. --Field Level Media

item.title: Drake Maye (3 TDs), Patriots stun Bills at home with late score
item.description: Drake Maye completed 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards and three touchdowns, including a late, go-ahead TD pass to Efton Chism III, to lead the New England Patriots to a 29-26 victory over the Buffalo Bills on Sunday in Orchard Park, N.Y.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Drake Maye completed 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards and three touchdowns, including a late, go-ahead TD pass to Efton Chism III, to lead the New England Patriots to a 29-26 victory over the Buffalo Bills on Sunday in Orchard Park, N.Y. Chism's leaping, one-handed 23-yard TD catch plus Maye's pass to Rhamondre Stevenson for the two-point conversion gave the Patriots a 29-26 lead with 1:50 to play. Craig Woodson intercepted a Josh Allen pass at the New England 19-yard line on the ensuing possession, and the Patriots (2-2) were able to run out the clock and hand Buffalo (3-1) its first loss in its new stadium. Allen was 23-of-33 passing for 253 yards and one touchdown. Buffalo's Keon Coleman caught six passes for 116 yards and a TD. James Cook rushed for 75 yards and a score. The Patriots struck first when Maye connected with Romeo Doubs (six receptions, 58 yards, two TDs) for a 14-yard touchdown pass with 7:01 left in the first quarter. The score capped a 12-play, 97-yard drive. Buffalo tied the game on Cook's 8-yard TD run plus Tyler Bass' extra point 45 seconds into the second quarter. New England regained the lead on Stevenson's 1-yard run with 5:38 left before halftime, but Buffalo responded when Allen scored from 2 yards away with one minute left. The TD gave Allen the most touchdowns from scrimmage (88) in franchise history, breaking a tie with Andre Reed and Thurman Thomas. It remained 14-14 until Bass made a 27-yard field goal with two seconds left in the half. The field goal was set up by Dee Alford's interception that he returned to the New England 9-yard line with nine seconds remaining. The interception came after Doubs lost control of the ball as he fell to the ground following a catch. The Patriots were up 21-17 after Doubs caught a 2-yard TD pass with 8:15 left in the third, but Buffalo made it 21-20 on Bass' 38-yard field goal with 11:07 to play in the game. The Bills regained their lead at 26-21 on Allen's 34-yard TD pass to Coleman with 4:27 left. The ensuing two-point conversion attempt failed. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jameis Winston, Giants outlast Cardinals to move to 3-1
item.description: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdown passes and the New York Giants outlasted the Arizona Cardinals 36-24 on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdown passes and the New York Giants outlasted the Arizona Cardinals 36-24 on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J. Winston overcame two interceptions and four sacks to complete 18 of 29 passes for 250 yards. He found tight end Theo Johnson on an 11-yard connection late in the third quarter for the go-ahead score. In a back-and-forth game with three lead changes and six turnovers, the Giants (3-1) had to climb out of a 14-3 first-quarter hole. New York turned things around with Winston's touchdown passes to Malachi Fields and Malik Nabers in the final 4:30 of the first half, which followed the second of three Dominic Zvada field goals. The Giants' halftime lead was cut to 19-17 when the Cardinals' Chad Ryland booted a 60-yard field goal as time expired. The Cardinals reclaimed the lead midway through the third quarter when Jacoby Brissett found a wide-open Elijah Higgins over the middle for a 2-yard touchdown pass to make it 24-19. But they couldn't come up with any more points as they ventured into Giants territory just once in their final four possessions. Arizona (1-3) lost its third straight game after a season-opening road win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett completed 21 of 35 passes for 166 yards with two touchdowns and three interceptions, including a pick-6 on the game's final play. Giants running back Cam Skattebo ran for a key first down with just over three minutes left to allow New York to take more time off the clock, but the Giants settled for a 52-yard field goal by Zvada with 2:11 to play. The Cardinals had one more chance. Deonte Banks was whistled for an 18-yard pass interference call on a pass intended for Marvin Harrison Jr., which moved the Cardinals down to the Giants' 4-yard line with 22 seconds to play. After Brissett threw three straight incomplete passes, Banks redeemed himself on fourth down by intercepting Brissett and returning it 98 yards for a touchdown as the clock ran out. The Cardinals lost starting offensive tackle Paris Johnson Jr. to injury on the final drive. Earlier in the game, right guard Isaiah Adams and safety Andrew Wingard (knee) were carted off. --Field Level Media

item.title: Com 1,23% das seções apuradas, Flávio lidera apuração com 48,85% dos votos contra 42,50% de Lula, mostra TSE
item.description: Com 1,23% das seções eleitorais apuradas nas eleições presidenciais deste domingo, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) liderava com 48,85% dos votos válidos, seguido pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) com 42,50%, de acordo com dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Com 1,23% das seções eleitorais apuradas nas eleições presidenciais deste domingo, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) liderava com 48,85% dos votos válidos, seguido pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) com 42,50%, de acordo com dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE). Para vencer a eleição já neste domingo, um candidato precisa conquistar mais de 50% dos votos válidos.

item.title: Lamar Jackson exits, Ravens hold on to beat Titans
item.description: Lamar Jackson threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns on 15-of-20 passing but exited early in the Ravens' 24-18 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday in Baltimore.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Lamar Jackson threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns on 15-of-20 passing but exited early in the Ravens' 24-18 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday in Baltimore. The Ravens (3-1) snapped a four-game losing streak in their home stadium but needed their defense to hang on after the Titans (0-4) held them scoreless in the second half without Jackson, who did not play after halftime. Jackson was sacked on Baltimore's final play of the second quarter by Jermaine Johnson II, who landed on Jackson's left ankle. Jackson was later seen on the sideline with his ankle wrapped. Tyler Huntley played the rest of the game and completed 8 of 9 passes for 63 yards and ran for 16 yards on four attempts. The Ravens were held scoreless after taking a 24-7 lead to the half. Cam Ward's 3-yard touchdown pass to Wan'Dale Robinson and two-point conversion pass to Gunnar Helm pulled the Titans within six with 1:12 left. But Malaki Starks recovered Tennessee's ensuing onside kick with 1:10 left and Baltimore ran out the clock. The Titans, who lost their first four games for the second consecutive season, were held to just a 33-yard field goal by Joey Slye in the second half until that late score. Tennessee committed two costly first-half turnovers -- an interception by Ward and a fumble after a catch by Carnell Tate -- which led to 10 points for the Ravens. Ward completed 20 of 31 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown and was intercepted on the Titans' first drive by Trenton Simpson. Tate caught nine passes for 145 yards. Baltimore also stopped Tennessee on fourth down at the Ravens' 2 with 8:16 left in the second quarter. Nnamdi Madubuike stopped Tony Pollard short of a touchdown that would have tied the game at 14. The Ravens responded with an eight-play, 98-yard drive that ended with Jackson finding Mark Andrews open in the end zone for a 3-yard touchdown to put Baltimore ahead 21-7. Derrick Henry beat his former team for the first time and finished with 73 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries. Zay Flowers caught eight passes for 118 yards and a touchdown. Baltimore kicker Tyler Loop continued his hot streak by making a 64-yard field goal as time expired in the first half. --Field Level Media

By Brendan O’Boyle, Luciana Magalhaes and Rodrigo Viga Gaier BRASILIA/SAO PAULO/RIO DE JANEIRO, Oct 4 (Reuters) – Polls began closing in Brazil on Sunday afternoon after voters queued in long lines to vote in the first round of a tight presidential election, following a campaign dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling.

The field of 13 candidates has been led by two clear frontrunners — leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, 80, who is seeking a fourth term, and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the 45-year-old son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who hopes to return his father’s right-wing movement to power.

A victory for the senator would extend a wave of wins across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with US President Donald Trump, while Lula’s reelection could create a headache for Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security.

Despite growing worries over Brazil’s public finances and sluggish economic growth, the campaign offered meager policy debate, as both leading candidates skipped the major TV debates.

All of Brazil’s states close polls at 5:00 p.m. Brasilia time (2000 GMT), though voters in line before this time will still be allowed to cast their vote. Results will be reported shortly after.

If no candidate wins more than 50% of valid votes, the top two will face off on October 25. Surveys show Lula and Flavio polling roughly even in a likely runoff.

While polls right up until Saturday showed Lula would likely lead the first round but not avoid a runoff, Flavio told journalists in Rio de Janeiro he was confident he could win the presidency in the first round, citing voters’ frustration with his chief opponent.

Flavio was counting on “a protest vote from people who would otherwise vote for another candidate but are opposed to Lula,” he said. “I hope it’s enough to secure a victory in the first round.”

Thaise Lima, a 41-year-old lawyer on her way to vote in Sao Paulo, said her main goal was to get Lula’s Workers Party out of office.

“I don’t think Flavio is the best candidate, but I might decide to vote for him in the next few minutes,” she said, adding that she wished psychiatrist and author Augusto Cury were a more viable candidate.

Fernando Tempel, 49, a management consultant, told Reuters he was voting for Flavio despite initially planning to vote for Romeu Zema, the former governor of Minas Gerais state.

OUTSIDE INTERFERENCE

On the other hand, Lula’s allies have warned that the Trump administration might refuse to recognize election results if he wins, pointing to an aborted effort to send US officials to Brazil.

“What is at stake is the future of Brazil,” Lula said after voting in Sao Bernardo do Campo, in Sao Paulo state.

Trump has not formally endorsed a candidate, though he hosted Senator Flavio Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly.

“I’m a little worried about everything that’s been happening recently, including internationally. I feel this election has had a lot of outside influence, more than in previous elections,” said Cristiano, 34, a doctor in Brasilia who voted for Lula and preferred to withhold his surname.

“We are confident in our President Lula, who will fight for national sovereignty,” said Pedro Palacio, 45, who was voting in Brasilia alongside his wife, Andreia, and their two sons and two dogs, all of whom wore outfits supporting the president.

As of Sunday afternoon, the election was proceeding normally, Brazil’s electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques said in a press conference.

“Teams monitoring international risks have not identified any risks whatsoever,” he said.

Reuters reported on Wednesday that Brazilian intelligence officials briefed a French and German delegation on alleged US and Russian interference before the election. The US has rejected claims of interference in Brazil’s affairs.

ECONOMIC HEADWINDS

Despite falling inequality and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over voters grappling with high living costs, heavy household debt and the threat of street crime and more pervasive gang activity.

Flavio Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns, while Lula has moved to ban online gambling and, as the race tightened, expanded welfare and proposed fresh debt relief for families.

Rising spending and public debt above 82% of GDP have stoked fiscal concerns that Brazil’s next president will need to address. The government lowered its economic growth forecasts for this year and next to just 2.0% and 2.3% respectively.

“I voted for Brazil to start growing again,” said Marciano de Souza e Silva, a 52-year-old public servant in Brasilia and former Lula voter who moved right, voting for Jair Bolsonaro in 2018 and 2022 and Flavio on Sunday.

“The best social program is one that encourages people to start businesses, to actually produce real wealth,” he said.

SCANDAL-PLAGUED CAMPAIGNS

Overshadowing the policy debate, a scandal surrounding the now-defunct Banco Master has engulfed much of Brazil’s political class and renewed public anger over corruption.

Daniel Vorcaro, who ran the bank, was arrested earlier this year and accused of a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme. The investigation has probed the banker’s ties to figures from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to Flavio Bolsonaro, who is being investigated for money laundering tied to the case by the federal police.

The candidate has denied any wrongdoing, although he confirmed raising millions of dollars from Vorcaro to make a movie about his father.

The banker’s connections to Moraes, widely perceived as a Lula ally, plunged the court into crisis a month before the vote, creating fresh problems for the president. Moraes has said the case against him is politically motivated for his role in the conviction of the elder Bolsonaro.

On Sunday, voters will also elect all 513 lower house members and two-thirds of the Senate, where some lawmakers have pushed to impeach Moraes.

item.title: Jordan Love, Packers' defense keep Bucs winless
item.description: Jordan Love threw two touchdown passes and the Green Bay Packers' defense picked off a pair of passes en route to a 17-14 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday in Tampa.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jordan Love threw two touchdown passes and the Green Bay Packers' defense picked off a pair of passes en route to a 17-14 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday in Tampa. Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards and Tucker Kraft had six catches for 42 yards and a score for the Packers (2-2), who moved to 2-0 on the road. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, making his first start, completed 19 of 27 passes for 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions for Tampa Bay (0-4), which remained the NFC's last winless team. Daniels also rushed for 55 yards playing in place of the injured Baker Mayfield. Leading 10-7 at halftime, Green Bay opened the second half with an eight-play scoring drive that Love capped with a 2-yard touchdown pass to Kraft. Daniels answered with the first touchdown pass of his career as he hit Kenneth Gainwell for a 10-yard score to cut the Buccaneers' deficit to 17-14 with 14:49 to play. Green Bay threatened to add on, but Kaleb Johnson lost a fumble that cornerback Zyon McCollum recovered at the Tampa Bay 4. The Buccaneers were forced to punt, but regained the ball with another takeaway as Jacob Parrish intercepted Love at the Tampa Bay 7 with 4:18 remaining. Tampa Bay advanced as far as the Packers' 46 on its last drive, but Keisean Nixon broke up a fourth-down pass with 1:25 remaining to clinch matters. Daniels was picked off on Tampa Bay's second drive. Evan Williams jumped a route and pulled in the interception at the Packers' 32. Green Bay took advantage as it pieced together a 16-play, 68-yard drive that chewed up more than nine minutes. Love threw a 2-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden for the game's first score. Tampa Bay evened the score on Sean Tucker's 2-yard rush with 5:13 remaining in the first half. Daniels threw his second interception with less than a minute left before halftime, this time to Edgerrin Cooper. Green Bay finished the half with a 58-yard field goal by Trey Smack for a 10-7 lead at the break. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kyren Williams, Rams run past Eagles
item.description: Kyren Williams rushed for two late touchdowns to rally the Los Angeles Rams to a 24-20 victory against the Eagles on a soggy Sunday afternoon in Philadelphia.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyren Williams rushed for two late touchdowns to rally the Los Angeles Rams to a 24-20 victory against the Eagles on a soggy Sunday afternoon in Philadelphia. Williams scored from 1 yard out with 3:59 left and from 7 yards out with 1:10 remaining to lift the Rams (2-2) over the Eagles (2-2), who had never trailed to that point. Byron Young sealed the win with two sacks on Philadelphia's final drive. Matthew Stafford overcame two first-half interceptions and finished with 317 yards on 32-of-51 passing. Puka Nacua had a touchdown run to go with 125 yards on nine catches and Williams gained 147 yards (80 rushing, 67 receiving) from scrimmage. Jalen Hurts threw two touchdowns to Darius Cooper and Philadelphia built a 20-10 lead by halftime, but the offense largely struggled after losing Saquon Barkley to an early injury and finished 0-for-12 on third-down conversions with only 172 yards of offense. Hurts completed 12 of 27 passes for 93 yards. Barkley went out with a right hamstring injury on the second snap of the game. The Eagles' short-handed offense was already playing without wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) and right tackle Lane Johnson (personal). The drive on which Barkley got hurt began with the Eagles' first takeaway of the season, an interception by Andrew Mukuba. It ended with Jake Elliott's 29-yard field goal. Philadelphia had been the only NFL team with zero takeaways and zero points in the opening quarter. The Rams made it 3-3 with a 40-yard field goal by Harrison Mevis late in the first quarter. Philadelphia built a 13-3 lead in the second quarter with a 56-yard field goal by Elliott and a juggling, 18-yard catch by Cooper in the end zone. Britain Covey set up Cooper's score with a 41-yard punt return. After missing the previous two games with hip and groin injuries, Nacua scored his third career rushing TD from 2 yards out just after the two-minute warning to pull the Rams within 13-10. Cooper DeJean's 25-yard interception return and a 25-yard pass-interference penalty against Trent McDuffie set up Cooper's second score. Hurts' 10-yard strike with three seconds left gave Philadelphia a 20-10 halftime lead. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kyle Monangai, Tyson Bagent stand out as Bears flatten Jets
item.description: Kyle Monangai rushed for 146 yards and two touchdowns and Tyson Bagent passed for 268 yards to boost the host Chicago Bears to a 23-12 victory against the New York Jets on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyle Monangai rushed for 146 yards and two touchdowns and Tyson Bagent passed for 268 yards to boost the host Chicago Bears to a 23-12 victory against the New York Jets on Sunday. Chicago (3-1) limited New York (1-3) to 157 total yards as the Jets lost their third game in a row. The Bears rolled up 492 yards of offense while collecting 34 first downs to the Jets' seven. Bagent finished 25-of-34 passing, Rome Odunze had six catches for 94 yards and Monangai finished with 30 carries. Jason Sanders connected on field goals of 36 and 30 yards for New York, which enjoyed a rare bright spot when safety Minkah Fitzpatrick picked off Bagent in the second quarter. That stopped a record drought of 21 games without an interception for the Jets, who snagged their first pick since Jan. 5, 2025. New York had three potential interceptions nullified by penalty. Bagent started one week after journeyman Case Keenum accounted for three total touchdowns while leading the Bears to a home victory against the Philadelphia Eagles, shining in his first start since December 2023. Bagent was active for the Philadelphia game after spending much of the previous week in concussion protocol. He started sharply against the Jets, completing his first five passes, including gains of 21 and 20 yards to Odunze and Luther Burden III on successive plays. Chicago marched 93 yards on 14 plays on the opening possession but didn't score, as Brandon Stephens stopped D'Andre Swift on fourth-and-goal from the 1-yard line. The Bears visited the end zone on their next possession, with Monangai converting on fourth-and-goal from the 1 with 23 seconds left in the first quarter. Cairo Santos followed Sanders' first field goal of the afternoon with separate 30-yard field goals over the final 2:29 of the half, giving the Bears a 13-3 edge at intermission. A Sanders field goal pulled the Jets within 13-6 midway through the third quarter before the Bears pulled away with 10 straight points, including a 5-yard Monangai touchdown run to cap a nine-play, 72-yard drive. Geno Smith connected with Isaiah Williams for a 58-yard touchdown pass with 9:16 left, but Sanders missed the point-after attempt. Smith was 8-of-15 passing for 119 yards and a touchdown. Braelon Allen gained 59 yards on 14 carries while Williams had two catches for 73 yards. Jets cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was ruled out with a concussion in the fourth quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jets capitalize on power plays, take down Red Wings
item.description: Kyle Connor scored two power-play goals and added an assist to lift the Winnipeg Jets to a 3-2 victory over the host Detroit Red Wings on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyle Connor scored two power-play goals and added an assist to lift the Winnipeg Jets to a 3-2 victory over the host Detroit Red Wings on Sunday afternoon. Cole Perfetti scored the other goal and had two assists, while Josh Morrissey added two assists for the Jets, who went 3-for-4 on the power play. Stuart Skinner made 33 saves in Winnipeg's first victory. The Jets lost to Boston in overtime in their season opener Friday. Viktor Arvidsson and Emmitt Finnie scored for the Red Wings and John Gibson stopped 24 shots. Former Detroit captain Dylan Larkin, who has requested a trade, missed the game with an upper-body injury. Forward Marco Kasper was also sidelined by an upper-body injury suffered during the team's 2-0 opening-night loss to the New York Rangers on Friday. Winnipeg goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, a teammate of Larkin's on the gold medal-winning Team USA at the 2026 Winter Olympics, was not with the team after being suspended for failing to show up for training camp. He has also requested a trade. The crowd was riled up with 7:50 left in the opening period, as the Jets' Tyrel Bauer and Wings' Keegan Kolesar dropped the gloves. Along with the fighting penalties, Kolesar was whistled for unsportsmanlike conduct, giving the Jets a power play. They cashed in on Perfetti's goal. Connor passed the puck to Perfetti and the puck was deflected up and over Gibson with 6:56 remaining in the period. At the same time as the goal, Detroit's J.T. Compher was whistled for unsportsmanlike conduct. Once again, Winnipeg converted its power play, as Connor skated to the net and flipped a backhander past Gibson with 5:24 left in the period. Gabriel Vilardi and Perfetti collected the assists. Connor's second power-play goal came after Lucas Raymond was penalized for holding. Connor collected a rebound in the right circle and rifled a shot past Gibson. With Dylan DeMelo in the penalty box for tripping, Arvidsson ended Detroit's drought when he scored in front off an Andrew Copp feed. Moritz Seider had the second assist. Finnie made it 3-2 at 4:56 of the third, converting in front off Michael Brandsegg-Nygard's pass from behind the net. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alaska LNG shipping savings justifies billions in investment, developer says
item.description: Alaska LNG's developer said the project's access to stranded natural gas and shorter shipping routes to Asia will make it competitive with US Gulf Coast rivals, despite questions from some analysts about the project's massive infrastructure costs.
item.dc:creator: Curtis Williams
item.content:encoded: Alaska LNG's developer said the project's access to stranded natural gas and shorter shipping routes to Asia will make it competitive with US Gulf Coast rivals, despite [USN:L1N45N10U TEXT:"questions"] from some analysts about the project's massive infrastructure costs. When the project is completed, the cost of shipping gas to Asia from Alaska's North Slope would be at least 65% cheaper than shipping LNG from the Gulf Coast, Tim Fitzpatrick, communications director for project developer Glenfarne, said on Sunday in an email to Reuters. The proposed project, [USN:S0N43J052 TEXT:"backed"] by President Donald Trump, would move gas from Alaska's North Slope through an 800-mile pipeline to a liquefied natural gas export plant in southern Alaska. A key question has been whether lower shipping costs justify the billions of dollars needed to build the infrastructure. Critics have pointed to the project's estimated cost of $44.5 billion to $54.5 billion, which translates to roughly $2.2 billion to $2.7 billion per million tons per annum (MTPA) of LNG capacity. That appears significantly higher than many recently approved Gulf Coast developments. But developer Glenfarne argues that the comparison is misleading because it includes the expense of pipeline and gas treatment infrastructure needed to bring stranded North Slope gas to market. The Alaska LNG project entails about $1.4 billion per MTPA in delivery costs, Fitzpatrick said. US LNG projects approved since Russia's invasion of Ukraine have generally been built at an average cost of about $1 billion per mtpa or less. Glenfarne argues the project's competitiveness should be measured by delivered LNG costs rather than upfront spending. The company, Fitzpatrick said, so far has identified customers for 13 million tons per year of LNG, and needs 16 million tons annually to support project financing. Trump on Friday said South Korea will help finance the Alaska LNG effort as part of a $200 billion package of investment in US projects. But Seoul quickly suggested that its role in the Alaska project is not yet set.

item.title: Austrian government's No. 2 figure says he will step down
item.description: Austrian Vice Chancellor Andreas Babler said on Sunday he would quit as the second-highest government official and as leader of the ruling Social Democratic Party next year, bowing to growing unrest within the party over its slide in opinion polls.
item.dc:creator: Francois Murphy
item.content:encoded: Austrian Vice Chancellor Andreas Babler said on Sunday he would quit as the second-highest government official and as leader of the ruling Social Democratic Party next year, bowing to growing unrest within the party over its slide in opinion polls. The Social Democrats are the second party in a three-way government led by conservative Chancellor Christian Stocker that was formed last year after the far-right Freedom Party (FPO) won the most seats in a parliamentary election for the first time but was unable to forge a ruling coalition. While the three-party government's formation shut the FPO out of power, the FPO has only gained ground in opinion polls since then. Its support is now running around 38%, more than the Social Democrats and Stocker's People's Party combined. Speculation about Babler's potential departure grew as the Social Democrats' support kept sliding. Recent opinion polls put it on 15%, a fall of about 6 points since the last parliamentary election in September 2024. "Public debates over who the leader should be are not good for political parties. Public disputes are not good for political parties," Babler told a press conference after a day of meetings among senior party figures, adding that the debate over whether he should quit was a distraction. "I am convinced this must end," he said. Finance Minister Markus Marterbauer, who is [USN:L1N43F08U TEXT:"undergoing treatment for cancer"], will replace Babler as vice chancellor early next year and Babler will step down as party leader at the same time, Babler said, adding that he could not say which week the change would happen in.

item.title: France's Schneider Electric nears $20 billion deal to buy US software group PTC, FT reports
item.description: France's Schneider Electric is nearing a deal to buy US software group PTC for about $20 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday citing people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France's Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) is nearing a deal to buy US software group PTC (PTC.O) for about $20 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday citing people with knowledge of the matter. A deal may be announced as soon as Monday, the newspaper said, adding that discussions between the two companies were ongoing and there was no certainty they would result in a deal. Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report. Schneider Electric and PTC did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment outside regular business hours. Boston-based PTC has a market value of $15.63 billion, according to LSEG data. In July, the company had lifted its [USN:L4N43V2I2 TEXT:"annual revenue forecast"] after third-quarter results, betting on strong demand for its core industrial software and artificial intelligence-powered tools.

item.title: Report: Seahawks to work out RB Joe Mixon
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks are bringing in free-agent running back Joe Mixon for a workout, Fox Sports reported Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Seattle Seahawks are bringing in free-agent running back Joe Mixon for a workout, Fox Sports reported Sunday. The reigning Super Bowl champions are looking to add backfield depth after placing rookie Jadarian Price (chest) on injured reserve Saturday. Seattle signed Velus Jones Jr. off its practice squad Saturday to take Price's spot on the roster. Zach Charbonnet (knee) will be eligible to return in Week 5. Mixon, 30, played his first seven seasons for the Cincinnati Bengals, eclipsing 1,000 rushing yards in four of them. During that span, he compiled 6,412 yards and 49 touchdowns rushing, to go with 283 receptions for 2,139 yards and 13 receiving touchdowns. In 2024, he joined the Houston Texans, rushing for 1,016 yards and 11 touchdowns in 14 games. He earned his second career Pro Bowl selection as a result. Mixon missed the 2025 season with a foot injury. The Texans released him last March. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bengals lose WRs Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor)
item.description: Along with losing All-Pro wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion in Sunday's home loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Cincinnati Bengals saw No. 2 receiver Tee Higgins leave the game with an adductor injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Along with losing All-Pro wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion in Sunday's home loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Cincinnati Bengals saw No. 2 receiver Tee Higgins leave the game with an adductor injury. Chase, who had three catches for 27 yards, was ruled out with a concussion after his head hit the turf early in the second quarter of the 22-17 loss. Higgins, who reeled in 11 receptions for 157 yards, exited in the fourth quarter and missed most of the Bengals' last possession that ended at the Jaguars' 12-yard line. In the second quarter, Chase caught a 4-yard pass from Joe Burrow then had his facemask grabbed and pulled by Jaguars cornerback Jarrian Jones. While Chase fell to the ground, linebacker Ventrell Miller dove into Chase and knocked the back of his helmet into the turf. Following a toe-tapping sideline grab late in the game, Higgins injured his adductor. He left briefly and returned for one play on the Bengals' final drive but was unable to continue. Chase, 26, has 21 receptions for 212 yards and three touchdowns over four games this season. In six NFL seasons, all with the Bengals, the five-time Pro Bowl selection has 541 receptions for 7,049 yards and 57 touchdowns. The Bengals selected him with the No. 5 overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft. Higgins, 27, has 25 receptions for 401 yards and one touchdown in four games this season. In his seventh season after Cincinnati selected him in the second round of the 2020 draft, Higgins has 414 catches for 5,842 yards and 46 touchdowns. He earned his first Pro Bowl selection last year, posting a career-high 11 touchdowns. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson (ankle) misses second half, reportedly day-to-day
item.description: Lamar Jackson missed the second half of the Baltimore Ravens' 24-18 win against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but NFL Network reported that he's believed to be day-to-day with a left ankle injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lamar Jackson missed the second half of the Baltimore Ravens' 24-18 win against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but NFL Network reported that he's believed to be day-to-day with a left ankle injury. Jackson was seen wearing a protective boot as he left the stadium, but Ravens coach Jesse Minter indicated that Jackson avoided a major injury. "He was just dealing with a little bit of an ankle," Minter said postgame. "I don't know enough about it right now, but we'll have to see where that's at." When asked whether Jackson could have returned to the game if Baltimore needed him, Minter said, "There were some talks about that. So, hopefully it's in a good spot." Jackson was initially ruled questionable to return after suffering the injury on his final play of the first half. The two-time MVP quarterback appeared to turn his left ankle when attempting to elude a sack by Jermaine Johnson II, who landed on the ankle as he fell to the ground. Tyler Huntley took over with the Ravens leading 24-7 coming out of halftime. Huntley completed 8 of 9 pass attempts for 63 yards and ran four times for 16 yards, but the Ravens were held scoreless in the half as the Titans made a comeback bid that fell short. Jackson completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns and was sacked twice in the first half. He also rushed twice for 20 yards. The Ravens also lost star cornerback Marlon Humphrey (calf), right guard Andrew Vorhees (foot) and tight end Durham Smythe (Achilles) throughout the course of the game. Minter had no additional information about their statuses postgame. --Field Level Media

item.title: Dustin May, Nick Pivetta named Game 3 starters in Brewers-Padres NLDS
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy said Sunday that right-hander Dustin May will start Game 3 of the National League Division Series against the San Diego Padres on Tuesday when the series shifts to San Diego.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE -- Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy said Sunday that right-hander Dustin May will start Game 3 of the National League Division Series against the San Diego Padres on Tuesday when the series shifts to San Diego. May will square off against right-hander Nick Pivetta, who was named the Padres' Game 3 starter by manager Craig Stammen on Sunday. "He's pitched fantastic against the Padres," Murphy said of May hours before Game 2 of the best-of-five series at American Family Field. "He's got experience and we brought him in to do that." The Brewers won the series opener 3-2 on Saturday. May is 3-5 with a 3.14 ERA in 16 career regular-season games (13 starts) against San Diego. He faced the Padres three times this season, twice with the St. Louis Cardinals and once with the Brewers. He went 1-1 with a 1.23 ERA in those three games, allowing four runs, three earned, in 22 innings. May (7-9, 4.70 ERA), whose postseason roster spot was not a certainty, has been inconsistent with Milwaukee since being acquired at the trade deadline from St. Louis along with reliever JoJo Romero. May was 2-2 with a 5.65 ERA in 10 starts for the Brewers. Home runs were an issue; he gave up seven in 36 2/3 innings after allowing seven in 109 innings for the Cardinals. May lasted more than 3 2/3 innings in just one of his five starts in September. In his last outing, he allowed two runs on three hits, including a homer, in three innings in a 3-2 win over St. Louis. May is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA in nine career postseason outings, including three starts, all with the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2019 and 2020. Pivetta (3-2, 2.86 ERA) was 2-0 with a 1.45 ERA in four September starts after missing most of the season with a right elbow injury. He made four starts before going on the IL in mid-April. Pivetta started Game 2 of the Padres' wild-card series against the Chicago Cubs on Wednesday, allowing one run on three hits in 3 1/3 innings. San Diego went on to win 4-1 and complete a two-game sweep of Chicago. Pivetta threw 66 pitches before giving way to the Padres' vaunted bullpen, which Murphy has called the best in baseball. Milwaukee earned a first-round bye and home-field advantage throughout the postseason after winning a franchise-record 103 games. San Diego entered the wild-card round having won 17 of its final 20 games. --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: Braves punt on LHP Chris Sale, turn to LHP Ray Kerr in Game 2 of NLDS
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Hoping to have left-hander Chris Sale available to start Game 2 of the National League Division Series on Sunday, the Atlanta Braves turned to left-hander Ray Kerr instead as their starter against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: LOS ANGELES -- Hoping to have left-hander Chris Sale available to start Game 2 of the National League Division Series on Sunday, the Atlanta Braves turned to left-hander Ray Kerr instead as their starter against the Los Angeles Dodgers. The Braves had been waiting on Sale's availability after the staff ace recorded the final four outs of the wild-card-round clincher against the Philadelphia Philles on Thursday. "We'll have some conversations about this," Braves manager Walt Weiss said after the Braves' 5-3 road loss in Game 1 of the best-of-five series on Saturday. "So, not sure who's going to start. That's where we're at right now." Sale's next opportunity to start a game will come in Game 3 on Tuesday at Atlanta. The Dodgers already named ace right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto to start that game, creating a matchup of dynamic starters. Sale and Yamamoto squared off Aug. 27, also at Atlanta, and the Braves walked away with a 1-0 victory to finish off a three-game series sweep behind a complete-game shutout from Sale. Kerr, 32, takes the mound after he started Thursday's wild-card clincher against the Phillies when he went 3 1/3 scoreless innings on one hit. Kerr had a 1.47 ERA in nine appearances (one start) for Atlanta during the regular season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Missouri rout of Florida shakes up AP Top 25; top teams unchanged
item.description: Missouri's surprise rout of Florida and Alabama's road blowout of Mississippi State on Saturday generated the most movement in the latest Associated Press Top 25.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Missouri's surprise rout of Florida and Alabama's road blowout of Mississippi State on Saturday generated the most movement in the latest Associated Press Top 25. The Tigers surged from 25th to 14th in the rankings after taking down the Gators 45-17 in Columbia, Mo. Florida tumbled from eighth to 16th one week after reaching the top 10 with a blowout win over Ole Miss. As for the Crimson Tide, they switched places with reigning national champion Indiana, moving into sixth thanks to their 56-23 shellacking of the then-No. 16 Bulldogs in Starkville, Miss. The Hoosiers dropped to seventh despite taking care of Rutgers 47-15. The top five remain unchanged: Texas, which was idle; Georgia, which pulled away in the second half to defeat Vanderbilt 38-14; Notre Dame, which struggled in beating North Carolina 37-26 on the road; Miami (Fla.), which went into Clemson and routed the Tigers 41-13 in prime time; and Ohio State, which toppled then-No. 14 Iowa 31-14 in Iowa City. The Longhorns received 61 of 70 first-place votes from the AP's media panel. Georgia received six first-place votes, Miami got two and Indiana got one. As for the rest of the top 10, BYU moved up from 10th to eighth after beating TCU 17-10 in Fort Worth; Ole Miss, which was idle, remained in ninth, and LSU inched up from 11th to 10th after blowing out FCS McNeese State 63-14. Florida, Mississippi State and Iowa were the only ranked teams to lose in Week 5. Mississippi State dropped to 16th and Iowa fell to 20th. No. 24 Kentucky used a two-point conversion in overtime to edge South Carolina 35-34 in Columbia, S.C., but the Wildcats fell out of the rankings anyway. Pitt, at 25th, took their place. The Panthers edged Virginia Tech 35-33 on Friday in a game marked by controversy. The ACC officials posted under the goal posts ruled a game-winning field-goal attempt by the Hokies no good as time expired. Replays made the call appear less clear. AP Top 25 1. Texas 2. Georgia 3. Notre Dame 4. Miami (Fla.) 5. Ohio State 6. Alabama 7. Indiana 8. BYU 9. Ole Miss 10. LSU 11. Texas Tech 12. Utah 13. Oregon 14. Missouri 15. Tennessee 16. Florida 17. Mississippi State 18. Oklahoma State 19. USC 20. Iowa 21. UCLA 22. Houston 23. Boise State 24. SMU 25. Pitt --Field Level Media

item.title: Vídeo não mostra helicópteros dos EUA no Brasil durante eleições
item.description: Um vídeo de supostos helicópteros dos Estados Unidos não tem relação com as eleições brasileiras que ocorrem neste domingo, ao contrário do que afirmam posts no Instagram. O registro está disponível na plataforma há mais de um mês e tem um rótulo indicando que as imagens foram criadas por IA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo de supostos helicópteros dos Estados Unidos não tem relação com as eleições brasileiras que ocorrem neste domingo, ao contrário do que afirmam posts no Instagram. O registro está disponível na plataforma há mais de um mês e tem um rótulo indicando que as imagens foram criadas por IA. Estes são os principais detalhes: As imagens parecem ter sido feitas a partir de um veículo em movimento, enquanto helicópteros militares sobrevoam uma área descampada. “Estamos chegando, Brasil”, narra um homem ao fundo. A mesma gravação circula no Instagram ao menos desde 19 de agosto de 2026, quando foi compartilhada com o aviso “Conteúdo de IA” e a localização “Estados Unidos da América”. “Eu ‘tava’ na estrada por aqui quando comecei a ver essa movimentação e pensei: ‘Rapaz… o Brasil vai receber visita!’”, diz a legenda da postagem , publicada no perfil de um brasileiro que diz morar nos EUA. O autor do post respondeu a um comentário que apontou o uso de IA que “você não sabe brincar, não, olha a legenda”. Até o momento, não há registros de que o governo dos EUA tenha enviado helicópteros ao Brasil em meio às eleições. Uma possível interferência dos EUA no pleito preocupa autoridades brasileiras e é alvo de uma investigação da Polícia Federal (PF). Veredicto: falso. O vídeo de supostos helicópteros dos EUA no Brasil nas vésperas das eleições circula desde agosto com um rótulo de IA. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .
